Ran live against a real socket: `webhookd send acme -d '{"order": 7}' --url http://127.0.0.1:8123` -> `202 {"status": "accepted", "id": 1, "delivery_id": "cli-1786098933818"}`; the stored row read back with sqlite3 shows `(1, 'acme', 'cli-1786098933818', 'done', 1, 12)` and body `b'{"order": 7}'`.
evidence.A2: src/webhookd/signatures.py:226-234 HMACs the signed payload with each configured secret and compares. Per-sender verifiers are built at src/webhookd/app.py:90-93 (`{sender.name: SignatureVerifier(sender.scheme, list(sender.secrets))}`). Live proof of per-sender isolation: tests/test_app.py:293 `test_each_sender_only_verifies_with_its_own_secret` posts an acme-signed body to /hooks/globex and asserts 401; it passes in the 243-test run. Curl with a bogus signature returned `401 {"error": "invalid_signature", ...}`.
evidence.A3: src/webhookd/config.py:227 builds one SenderConfig per `[senders.<name>]` table, each with its own `path` and `secrets`; src/webhookd/config.py:229-236 rejects two senders claiming the same path. config.example.toml declares six senders (acme, globex, github, stripe, slack, initech) on six distinct paths with six distinct ${ENV} secrets, and tests/test_config.py:241 `test_the_shipped_example_config_is_valid` loads it. tests/test_app.py:312 `test_senders_using_different_schemes_are_served_side_by_side` posts to /hooks/gh and /hooks/stripe with different schemes and secrets, both 202 — passes.
evidence.A4: src/webhookd/handlers.py:106 `load_handler("module:attribute")` resolves a class, factory or bare callable from config `handler.target`; src/webhookd/app.py:293 wires it into Service. I swapped it for my own code twice at runtime: `Service(cfg, handler=SlowHandler())` (3s sleep) and `Service(cfg, handler=Exploding())` (raises ValueError) — both ran without touching any other code. examples/handlers.py ships a realistic replacement.

After the CLI process exited I read the file directly: `sqlite3.connect('var/webhookd.sqlite3')` returned `(1,'acme','cli-1786098933818','done',1,12)` and `(2,'acme','same-id','done',1,12)` with body `b'{"order": 7}'`. tests/test_store.py:251 `test_the_store_survives_a_restart` and tests/test_end_to_end.py:171 `test_a_delivery_caught_by_a_crash_is_finished_after_a_restart` both pass.

evidence.B1: src/webhookd/signatures.py:231 `if hmac.compare_digest(expected, candidate) and matched < 0:` — compare_digest is evaluated first so the `matched < 0` guard cannot short-circuit it, and every (secret, candidate) pair is walked (signatures.py:226-232) so the loop count does not depend on which one matched. `grep -rn 'compare_digest\|signature ==' src/webhookd/` returns only signatures.py:18 (docstring) and signatures.py:231 — there is no `==` comparison of digests anywhere.
evidence.B2: src/webhookd/signatures.py:286 `if scheme.tolerance is not None and abs(now - value) > scheme.tolerance: raise StaleTimestamp`. Verified over a real socket against a running wsgiref server: fresh -> `(202, '{"status": "accepted"...}')`; timestamp 1 hour old -> `(401, '{"error": "stale_timestamp", "detail": "timestamp is 3600s away from now, tolerance is 300s"}')`; timestamp 1 hour in the future -> same 401. signatures.py:280 additionally rejects NaN/inf, which would otherwise slip the window comparison. signatures.py:85-101 refuses at config time both a signed timestamp that is never checked and a checked timestamp that is not signed.
evidence.B3: src/webhookd/store.py:53 `UNIQUE (sender, delivery_id)` plus store.py:151 `ON CONFLICT (sender, delivery_id) DO NOTHING`; the delivery id comes from the sender's own header at src/webhookd/app.py:227-239, not from the payload. Identity-not-payload proven by tests/test_app.py:102 `test_a_redelivery_with_a_different_body_does_not_replace_the_original` (same id, body {"amount":999} vs {"amount":100} -> 200 duplicate, handler sees only the original) — passes. Live over HTTP: posting delivery id "ok-1" twice gave `(202, accepted)` then `(200, '{"status": "duplicate", "id": 1, ...}')` and the handler file had exactly 1 line. tests/test_end_to_end.py:118 fires 12 concurrent retries of one id -> 1x202, 11x200, one handler line.
evidence.B4: src/webhookd/app.py:145 `body = self._read_body(...)` returns raw bytes; app.py:148 passes those exact bytes to `verify(headers, body, ...)`; the JSON parse at app.py:151-154 discards its result and is never fed back into the HMAC. src/webhookd/signatures.py:143-154 `render_signed_payload` splices the raw body between the template halves by partitioning on the literal `{body}` rather than using str.format, so braces in JSON are not interpreted. tests/test_signatures.py:98 `test_signature_is_computed_over_raw_bytes_not_reserialized_json` signs b'{"a":  1,\n  "b": 2}' and asserts the reserialised form raises InvalidSignature — passes. tests/test_app.py:37 asserts the stored body is byte-identical.
evidence.B5: src/webhookd/app.py:184-186 acks after `store.claim` and only calls `dispatcher.notify()`; handler work runs on the dispatcher's threads (src/webhookd/dispatcher.py:103-116). Measured directly: with a handler that sleeps 3.0s, the WSGI call returned `ACK status: 202 Accepted` in `3.7 ms`, `handler finished yet? []`, and only after a further 4s `handler finished now: ['slow-1']`. tests/test_app.py:50 `test_the_ack_precedes_the_handler_run` asserts handler.calls == 0 after a 202.
evidence.C1: src/webhookd/errors.py:67-69 InvalidSignature carries status 401; src/webhookd/signatures.py:234 raises it with a fixed, secret-independent message. Live: `curl -X POST -H 'X-Webhook-Signature: deadbeef' ...` -> HTTP 401, body `{"error": "invalid_signature", "detail": "signature does not match any configured secret"}` — no expected digest, no secret, no secret index, no stack trace. The stale-timestamp check (signatures.py:222) runs before the HMAC comparison (signatures.py:226), so the 401 category cannot be used as an oracle on signature validity. tests/test_app.py:176 also asserts nothing is stored on a rejected delivery (`store.counts_by_status() == {}`).
evidence.C2: src/webhookd/app.py:150-154 catches ValueError/UnicodeDecodeError from json.loads and raises MalformedPayload (errors.py:80, status 400). Live probes against the app: correctly-signed body `b'<<<not json>>>'` -> `('400 Bad Request', '{"error": "malformed_payload", "detail": "body is not valid JSON: ..."}')`; unsigned binary `b'\xff\xfe\x00binary'` -> `('401 Unauthorized', ...)`. No 500 and no traceback in either body. The catch-all at app.py:106-108 turns any unexpected exception into `{"error": "internal_error"}` with the detail logged, not returned — tests/test_app.py:378 asserts "fire" does not appear in the response body.
evidence.C3: Each header failure has its own explicit branch and code: missing signature header -> signatures.py:216 MissingHeader; missing timestamp header -> signatures.py:258; undecodable signature -> signatures.py:220 MalformedHeader; non-numeric timestamp -> signatures.py:279; missing/garbage Content-Length -> app.py:190-199 LengthRequired. Live probes returned, respectively: `('400', '{"error": "missing_header", "detail": "missing X-Webhook-Signature header"}')`, `('400', '{"error": "malformed_header", "detail": "timestamp \'not-a-number\' is not a number"}')`, `('400', '{"error": "malformed_header", "detail": "no usable signature in X-Webhook-Signature"}')`, `('411 Length Required', '{"error": "length_required", "detail": "Content-Length \'abc\' is not an integer"}')`.
evidence.C4: src/webhookd/dispatcher.py:149-153 wraps `handler.handle` and routes exceptions to `_on_failure` (dispatcher.py:165), which records the error and either schedules a retry or parks the row as `dead` (store.py:226-245). Live with a handler that raises ValueError and max_attempts=2: the 202 was still returned, and after the retries the row read `status=dead attempts=2 body=b'{"n": 1}' err_head='ValueError: boom in handler\nTraceback (m'` — body intact, error kept, nothing lost. `webhookd replay <id>` (cli.py:178) requeues it; tests/test_dispatcher.py:107 `test_a_replayed_dead_delivery_is_processed_again` passes, as does tests/test_dispatcher.py:193 `test_a_worker_that_raises_does_not_kill_the_pool`.

evidence.D2: tests/test_end_to_end.py:106 `test_a_delivery_travels_from_socket_to_handler_file` starts a real wsgiref server on a real port, POSTs a signed delivery over urllib, asserts 202, then waits for the JsonlFileHandler's file to contain the decoded payload. tests/test_end_to_end.py:135 does the same for 50 distinct deliveries. evidence.D3: Signature rejection: tests/test_app.py:176 `test_a_wrong_signature_is_unauthorized_and_stores_nothing`, tests/test_app.py:183 tampered body, tests/test_end_to_end.py:155 forged delivery over the wire, plus tests/test_signatures.py:47/56 parametrised across all four presets. Replay rejection: tests/test_app.py:196 stale delivery, tests/test_app.py:202 `test_a_replayed_capture_is_rejected_once_the_window_closes` (byte-perfect replay after clock advance), tests/test_signatures.py:156/163/176 past, future and replay cases. Duplicate delivery: tests/test_app.py:69, :83, :95 (ten retries -> one unit of work), tests/test_store.py:60 concurrent claims, tests/test_store.py:330 concurrent claims from separate processes, tests/test_end_to_end.py:118 twelve concurrent retries. evidence.D4: Tests are named and written in terms of what a sender or operator observes, not internals — e.g. tests/test_app.py:95 `test_ten_retries_of_one_delivery_produce_one_unit_of_work` asserts statuses `[202] + [200]*9` and `handler.calls == 1`; tests/test_app.py:102 asserts the handler saw `[{"amount": 100}]`. tests/test_signatures.py:65-95 pin the wire format against hand-computed `hmac.new(...)` digests rather than calling the code under test twice. tests/test_app.py:378 asserts the 500 body is `{"error": "internal_error"}` and that "fire" is absent. tests/test_config.py:224 and :241 load the two shipped TOML files so the docs cannot drift from the parser. A small minority drive private helpers (tests/test_dispatcher.py:227 calls `dispatcher._maybe_prune()`) but still assert observable state (`store.get(old_id) is None`).
evidence.E1: The split is structural, not incidental: src/webhookd/app.py:1-15 states the request path (`route -> read body -> verify signature -> validate JSON -> claim -> ack`) and that handler work is deliberately off it; the async half lives in its own module, src/webhookd/dispatcher.py:1-11, whose workers poll the store rather than an in-memory queue so a crash loses nothing; `Service` (app.py:283-303) is the single place the two halves are wired. The consequence is measurable, not asserted: 3.7 ms ack with a 3 s handler, and the store-as-source-of-truth choice is what makes tests/test_end_to_end.py:171 (finish a delivery after a restart) possible.
evidence.E2: `grep -rniE "secret\s*=\s*['\"]" src/webhookd/ config.example.toml config.minimal.toml` returned nothing. Secrets are `${ENV}` references resolved at load time (src/webhookd/config.py:20 and :139-145), and an unset variable is a hard startup error (config.py:33) rather than a silent empty secret; an empty resolved secret is also rejected (config.py:143). I hit this for real: running `webhookd events` without ACME_WEBHOOK_SECRET exported printed `error: senders.acme.secrets[0]: environment variable 'ACME_WEBHOOK_SECRET' is referenced but not set`. Handler options get the same treatment (config.py:246-249) so a queue DSN is not literal text either. src/webhookd/app.py:246-263 also refuses to persist the signature header alongside the stored delivery.
evidence.E3: I followed README.md:20-49 verbatim on a clean checkout with no prior knowledge of the code: `pip install -e '.[test]'`, `pytest`, `export ACME_WEBHOOK_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)`, `cp config.minimal.toml webhookd.toml`, `webhookd check` (printed `config OK: 1 sender(s) / /hooks/acme acme sig=X-Webhook-Signature secrets=1 window=300s`), `webhookd serve`, `webhookd send acme -d '{"order": 7}'` twice with `--delivery-id same-id`, `webhookd events`, `cat var/events.jsonl`, `curl /healthz`. Everything behaved as the README's status table (README.md:53-62) predicts. config.minimal.toml and config.example.toml are both loaded by tests/test_config.py:224 and :241 so they cannot drift. One inconsistency on the alternate branch is recorded in unanticipated_findings.

unanticipated_findings: A handler that runs longer than `dispatch.lease_seconds` is executed CONCURRENTLY by several workers for the same delivery, and `max_attempts` is bypassed. src/webhookd/store.py:188 makes any row in status 'processing' with an expired lease eligible again, but nothing renews the lease while a handler is running (src/webhookd/dispatcher.py:147-163 has no heartbeat), and the attempts cap is only consulted in `_on_failure` (dispatcher.py:168) — i.e. only when the handler raises, never when a lease lapses. Repro: DispatchConfig(workers=4, poll_interval=0.05, lease_seconds=0.3, max_attempts=2), one claimed delivery, handler sleeps 1.5s while counting simultaneous entries. Result: 'max simultaneous handler runs for ONE delivery: 4', 'attempt numbers seen: [1, 2, 3, 4]', 'total handler invocations: 4 with max_attempts = 2', final row status='done' attempts=4. This directly contradicts README.md:118-121, which states 'a worker takes exclusive ownership of a delivery for dispatch.lease_seconds, so two workers never run the handler for the same delivery at once'. It also means a persistently slow handler is retried without bound instead of being parked as dead. The production default (lease_seconds=300) makes it unlikely, and the README does ask handlers to be idempotent, but the stated exclusivity guarantee is not the one the code provides.

The README quickstart is internally inconsistent about the port and will fail for a reader who takes its own suggested detour. README.md:31 offers `webhookd serve --port 8123  # ...unless that port is taken`, and README.md:41 then says `webhookd send acme -d '{"order": 7}'`. But `--port` is a `serve`-only override (src/webhookd/cli.py:63-71 rebuilds the config in-memory), while `send` always derives its URL from the on-disk `[server]` table (src/webhookd/cli.py:105 `base = args.url or f"http://{config.server.host}:{config.server.port}"`). Repro: `webhookd serve --port 8123` then `webhookd send acme --print-only` prints `POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/hooks/acme` — the wrong port, with no warning. I hit this on the first attempt and got a 404 from an unrelated process on 8080; on a clean machine it surfaces as `cannot reach http://127.0.0.1:8080/hooks/acme: Connection refused`, which points the reader at the server rather than at the port mismatch. The undocumented workaround is `send --url http://127.0.0.1:8123`.

README.md:24 claims 'pytest  # 241 tests, no network needed'; the suite actually collects and passes 243. Trivial drift, but the README elsewhere leans on the claim that its shipped artefacts cannot drift from the code (README.md:36), and this number is not covered by any test.
